name: Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

cards.term: What is a chemical bond?
cards.definition: The attractive force that holds atoms or ions together in a chemical species

cards.term: Why do atoms form bonds at all?
cards.definition: To lower the energy of the system and become more stable

cards.term: What was the Lewis 'kernel'?
cards.definition: The nucleus + inner electrons of an atom (positively charged)

cards.term: What do the dots in a Lewis symbol stand for?
cards.definition: The valence electrons

cards.term: How do you get the group valence from a Lewis symbol?
cards.definition: Number of dots, or 8 − number of dots

cards.term: What is electrovalence?
cards.definition: The number of unit charges on the ion (e.g. Ca²⁺ → 2)

cards.text: Octet rule: atoms combine by {{c1::transfer}} or {{c2::sharing}} of valence electrons so as to have an {{c3::octet}} in their valence shells.

cards.term: Who introduced the term 'covalent bond'?
cards.definition: Langmuir

cards.term: Name a molecule with two double bonds and one with a triple bond.
cards.definition: CO₂ (two C=O); N₂ or C₂H₂ (triple)

cards.term: In a Lewis structure, which atom usually goes in the centre?
cards.definition: The least electronegative atom

cards.term: How do charges change the electron count for a Lewis structure?
cards.definition: Add 1 e⁻ per negative charge; subtract 1 e⁻ per positive charge

cards.term: Lewis structure of CO: what bond joins C and O?
cards.definition: A triple bond, with one lone pair on each atom

cards.term: Formula for formal charge on an atom in a Lewis structure?
cards.definition:
Formal charge \(= V - L - \tfrac{1}{2}S\)
V = valence e⁻ of free atom, L = lone-pair e⁻, S = shared (bonding) e⁻

cards.term: Formal charges on the three O atoms of O₃?
cards.definition: Central O: +1; double-bonded end O: 0; single-bonded end O: −1

cards.term: Which Lewis structure is usually the lowest-energy one?
cards.definition: The one with the smallest formal charges

cards.term: Do formal charges show real charge separation?
cards.definition: No. They only help track valence electrons

cards.term: Give three molecules with an incomplete octet on the central atom.
cards.definition: LiCl, BeH₂, BCl₃ (also AlCl₃, BF₃)

cards.term: Give two odd-electron molecules.
cards.definition: NO and NO₂

cards.term: Why can third-period elements have an expanded octet?
cards.definition: They have d orbitals available for bonding

cards.term: Give three examples of an expanded octet.
cards.definition: PF₅, SF₆, H₂SO₄

cards.term: Name a sulphur compound where S obeys the octet rule.
cards.definition: SCl₂

cards.term: Which noble gas compounds challenge the octet rule?
cards.definition: XeF₂, KrF₂, XeOF₂

cards.term: Two more drawbacks of the octet theory?
cards.definition: It does not explain shapes of molecules, or their relative stability (energy)

cards.term: Which elements form ionic bonds most easily?
cards.definition: Low ionisation enthalpy (metal) + highly negative electron gain enthalpy (non-metal)

cards.term: Which common cation is made only of non-metals?
cards.definition: NH₄⁺ (ammonium)

cards.term: Is ionisation always endothermic?
cards.definition: Yes. Electron gain can be exothermic or endothermic

cards.term: What truly decides the stability of an ionic compound?
cards.definition: Its lattice enthalpy, not just reaching an octet

cards.term: Define lattice enthalpy.
cards.definition: Energy needed to completely separate 1 mol of a solid ionic compound into gaseous ions

cards.term: Lattice enthalpy of NaCl?
cards.definition: 788 kJ mol⁻¹

cards.term: Na → Na⁺ costs 495.8 kJ/mol and Cl → Cl⁻ releases only 348.7 kJ/mol. Why does NaCl still form?
cards.definition: The lattice enthalpy released (788 kJ mol⁻¹) more than compensates

cards.term: Define bond length.
cards.definition: Equilibrium distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms

cards.term: Bond length R of molecule AB in terms of covalent radii?

cards.text: Covalent radius is half the distance between two similar atoms bonded {{c1::in the same molecule}}; van der Waals radius is half the distance between two similar atoms {{c2::in separate molecules}} in a solid.

cards.term: Which is larger for chlorine: covalent or van der Waals radius?
cards.definition: van der Waals (180 pm vs 99 pm)

cards.term: Define bond enthalpy.
cards.definition: Energy to break 1 mol of bonds of a type between two atoms in the gaseous state

cards.term: Bond enthalpies: H2, O2, N2, HCl

cards.term: Why is average bond enthalpy used for polyatomic molecules like H₂O?
cards.definition: Breaking successive O–H bonds needs different energies (502 vs 427 kJ mol⁻¹)

cards.term: Average O–H bond enthalpy in water?
cards.definition: \(\frac{502 + 427}{2} = \) 464.5 kJ mol⁻¹

cards.term: Bond order in the Lewis picture?
cards.definition: The number of bonds between the two atoms

cards.term: Which species share bond order 3 by being isoelectronic?
cards.definition: N₂, CO, NO⁺

cards.term: Which species share bond order 1 by being isoelectronic?
cards.definition: F₂ and O₂²⁻

cards.text: As bond order increases, bond enthalpy {{c1::increases}} and bond length {{c2::decreases}}.

cards.term: Both O–O bonds in O₃ are 128 pm. How does this compare with single and double bonds?
cards.definition: Between O–O (148 pm) and O=O (121 pm)

cards.term: What is a resonance hybrid?
cards.definition: The single real structure that the canonical forms together describe

cards.term: How is resonance shown?
cards.definition: With a double-headed arrow (↔)

cards.term: How does resonance affect energy?
cards.definition: It stabilises the molecule: the hybrid has lower energy than any canonical form

cards.term: Do canonical forms really exist?
cards.definition: No. The molecule does not switch between them, and they are not in equilibrium

cards.term: How many canonical forms does CO₃²⁻ have, and how do its C–O bonds compare?
cards.definition: Three; all C–O bonds are equivalent

cards.term: C–O bond length in CO₂ (115 pm) lies between which two values?
cards.definition: C=O 121 pm and C≡O 110 pm

cards.term: Which is a non-polar covalent bond: H–H or H–F?
cards.definition: H–H (identical atoms share equally)

cards.term: Formula and unit of dipole moment?
cards.definition:
\(\mu = Q \times r\)
Unit: debye (D), 1 D = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C m

cards.term: Is dipole moment a scalar or a vector?
cards.definition: Vector

cards.term: In the chemist's crossed arrow for a dipole, where are the cross and the head?
cards.definition: Cross on the positive end, head on the negative end

cards.term: Dipole moment of H₂O?
cards.definition: 1.85 D (bent, H–O–H 104.5°)

cards.term: Why is the dipole moment of BeF₂ zero?
cards.definition: Linear: two equal bond dipoles cancel

cards.term: Why is the dipole moment of BF₃ zero though B–F bonds are polar?
cards.definition: Trigonal planar at 120°: the three bond moments sum to zero

cards.term: Why is μ(NH₃) greater than μ(NF₃)?
cards.definition: In NH₃ the lone-pair dipole points the same way as the N–H bond moments; in NF₃ it points opposite to the N–F moments

cards.term: Dipole moments of NH₃ and NF₃?
cards.definition: NH₃: 1.47 D; NF₃: 0.23 D

cards.term: Order of dipole moments: HF, HCl, HBr, HI?
cards.definition: HF > HCl > HBr > HI (1.78 > 1.07 > 0.79 > 0.38 D)

cards.term: CH₄ and CCl₄ have μ = 0. What is μ of CHCl₃?
cards.definition: 1.04 D

cards.text: Fajans' rules: covalent character of an ionic bond increases with a {{c1::smaller}} cation, a {{c2::larger}} anion, and a {{c3::greater charge}} on the cation.

cards.term: Which is more polarising for the same size and charge: a transition-metal cation or an alkali metal cation?
cards.definition: Transition-metal type, (n−1)dⁿns⁰

cards.term: Who proposed VSEPR theory, and who refined it?
cards.definition: Sidgwick and Powell (1940); refined by Nyholm and Gillespie (1957)

cards.term: According to VSEPR, what decides the shape of a molecule?
cards.definition: The number of valence shell electron pairs (bonded + lone) around the central atom

cards.term: How does VSEPR treat a double or triple bond?
cards.definition: As a single super pair

cards.term: Order of electron-pair repulsions?
cards.definition: lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp

cards.term: Why do lone pairs repel more than bond pairs?
cards.definition: A lone pair is held by one nucleus only, so it spreads out and takes more space

cards.term: VSEPR: geometry with no lone pairs
cards.definition: AB₂ · BeCl₂: Linear, 180°; AB₃ · BF₃: Trigonal planar, 120°; AB₄ · CH₄: Tetrahedral, 109.5°; AB₅ · PCl₅: Trigonal bipyramidal; AB₆ · SF₆: Octahedral

cards.term: H–N–H angle in NH₃ and why?
cards.definition: 107° (from 109.5°): lp–bp repulsion > bp–bp

cards.term: Why is the bond angle in H₂O (104.5°) less than in NH₃ (107°)?
cards.definition: H₂O has two lone pairs, and lp–lp repulsion is strongest

cards.term: In SF₄, is the lone pair axial or equatorial, and why?
cards.definition: Equatorial: only two lp–bp repulsions at 90° (vs three if axial)

cards.term: In ClF₃, where do the two lone pairs sit?
cards.definition: Equatorial positions, giving a T-shape

cards.term: For which elements does VSEPR predict shapes especially well?
cards.definition: p-block compounds

cards.term: Who introduced valence bond theory?
cards.definition: Heitler and London (1927), developed by Pauling

cards.term: Why does H₂ form when two H atoms approach?
cards.definition: New attractive forces exceed the new repulsive ones, so energy falls to a minimum

cards.term: Bond length and bond enthalpy of H₂?
cards.definition: 74 pm; 435.8 kJ mol⁻¹

cards.term: What decides the strength of a covalent bond in VB theory?
cards.definition: The extent of overlap: greater overlap, stronger bond

cards.term: When is an overlap positive (bond-forming)?
cards.definition: The orbitals have the same sign (phase) and orientation

cards.term: What H–C–H angle would simple (unhybridised) overlap predict for CH₄?
cards.definition: 90° (but the real angle is 109.5°)

cards.term: How is a σ bond formed?
cards.definition: Head-on (axial) overlap along the internuclear axis

cards.term: Which overlaps can give a σ bond?
cards.definition: s–s, s–p, p–p (head-on)

cards.term: How is a π bond formed?
cards.definition: Sidewise overlap: orbital axes parallel, perpendicular to the internuclear axis

cards.term: Which is stronger, σ or π, and why?
cards.definition: σ. Its orbitals overlap to a larger extent

cards.term: Can a π bond exist without a σ bond between two atoms?
cards.definition: No. π bonds form in addition to a σ bond

cards.term: With x as the internuclear axis, which pair cannot form a σ bond: 1s+1s, 1s+2pₓ, 2p_y+2p_y, 1s+2s?
cards.definition: 2p_y + 2p_y (sidewise → π)

cards.term: Number of σ and π bonds in C₂H₂ and C₂H₄?
cards.definition: C₂H₂: 3σ, 2π; C₂H₄: 5σ, 1π

cards.term: Who introduced hybridisation?
cards.definition: Pauling

cards.term: Define hybridisation.
cards.definition: Intermixing of orbitals of slightly different energies to form a new set of orbitals of equivalent energy and shape

cards.term: How many hybrid orbitals form from n atomic orbitals?
cards.definition: n (always equal)

cards.text: Conditions for hybridisation: only {{c1::valence shell}} orbitals mix; they must have {{c2::almost equal energy}}; promotion of electrons is {{c3::not essential}}.

cards.term: Can filled orbitals take part in hybridisation?
cards.definition: Yes. Not only half-filled ones

cards.term: sp, sp2, sp3: s-character and angle
cards.definition: sp: 50% s · 180° · linear; sp²: 33% s · 120° · trigonal planar; sp³: 25% s · 109.5° · tetrahedral

cards.term: Other name for sp hybridisation?
cards.definition: Diagonal hybridisation

cards.term: Hybridisation and shape of BeCl₂?
cards.definition: sp, linear (180°)

cards.term: Hybridisation and shape of BCl₃?
cards.definition: sp², trigonal planar (120°)

cards.term: Hybridisation of N in NH₃ and O in H₂O?
cards.definition: Both sp³ (lone pairs in hybrid orbitals)

cards.term: Ethane: C–C and C–H bond lengths?
cards.definition: C–C 154 pm (sp³–sp³); C–H 109 pm

cards.term: Ethene: what makes up the C=C bond?
cards.definition: One sp²–sp² σ + one π (from unhybridised 2p orbitals)

cards.term: Bond angles in ethene?
cards.definition: H–C–H 117.6°; H–C–C 121°

cards.term: What makes up the C≡C bond in ethyne?
cards.definition: 1 σ (sp–sp) + 2 π

cards.term: Why is no hybridisation of 3p, 3d and 4s possible?
cards.definition: The energy gap between 3p and 4s is significant

cards.term: d-orbital hybridisation: shapes and examples
cards.definition: dsp²: Square planar · [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻; sp³d: Trigonal bipyramidal · PCl₅; sp³d²: Square pyramidal · BrF₅ / octahedral · SF₆; d²sp³: Octahedral · [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺

cards.term: In PCl₅, how do equatorial and axial bonds differ?
cards.definition: Equatorial: three at 120°. Axial: two at 90° to that plane, longer and weaker

cards.term: Why are axial bonds in PCl₅ longer than equatorial ones?
cards.definition: Axial bond pairs suffer more repulsion from equatorial bond pairs

cards.term: Hybridisation and geometry of SF₆?
cards.definition: sp³d², regular octahedral

cards.term: AlCl₃ + Cl⁻ → AlCl₄⁻: change in hybridisation of Al?
cards.definition: sp² → sp³

cards.term: BF₃ + NH₃ → F₃B–NH₃: change in hybridisation of B and N?
cards.definition: B: sp² → sp³; N: stays sp³

cards.term: Who developed molecular orbital theory?
cards.definition: F. Hund and R.S. Mulliken (1932)

cards.term: Atomic orbital vs molecular orbital: how many nuclei influence the electron?
cards.definition: AO: monocentric (one nucleus). MO: polycentric

cards.term: Two atomic orbitals combine. How many MOs form?
cards.definition: Two: one bonding, one antibonding

cards.term: LCAO expressions for σ and σ*?
cards.definition:
\(\sigma = \psi_A + \psi_B\)
\(\sigma^* = \psi_A - \psi_B\)

cards.text: A bonding MO forms by {{c1::constructive}} interference; an antibonding MO by {{c2::destructive}} interference.

cards.term: What lies between the nuclei in an antibonding MO?
cards.definition: A nodal plane (zero electron density)

cards.text: Conditions for LCAO: combining AOs must have {{c1::the same or nearly the same energy}}, {{c2::the same symmetry about the molecular axis}}, and {{c3::maximum overlap}}.

cards.term: Can 2p_z of one atom combine with 2pₓ of the other (z = molecular axis)?
cards.definition: No. Different symmetry

cards.term: Which MOs are symmetrical about the bond axis: σ or π?
cards.definition: σ (π are not)

cards.text: For {{c1::B₂, C₂ and N₂}}, the π2p MOs lie {{c2::below}} σ2p_z; for O₂ and F₂, σ2p_z lies below π2p.

cards.term: Bond order formula in MO theory?
cards.definition: Bond order \(= \tfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\)

cards.term: What bond order means a molecule cannot exist?
cards.definition: Zero or negative (N_b ≤ N_a)

cards.term: When is a molecule paramagnetic in MO terms?
cards.definition: When one or more MOs are singly occupied (unpaired electrons)

cards.term: Bond order of He₂, and does it exist?
cards.definition: 0, so it does not exist

cards.term: Does Be₂ exist?
cards.definition: No. Bond order 0

cards.term: Bond order and magnetism of Li₂?
cards.definition: 1; diamagnetic (exists in the vapour phase)

cards.term: What is unusual about the double bond in C₂?
cards.definition: Both bonds are π bonds (no σ)

cards.term: Which of B₂ to F₂ has the highest bond enthalpy?
cards.definition: N₂ (945 kJ mol⁻¹, bond order 3)

cards.term: To which atoms must H be bonded to form hydrogen bonds?
cards.definition: Highly electronegative F, O or N

cards.term: Define hydrogen bond.
cards.definition: The attractive force binding the H atom of one molecule to an electronegative atom (F, O, N) of another

cards.term: Is a hydrogen bond weaker or stronger than a covalent bond?
cards.definition: Weaker

cards.term: Is a hydrogen bond weaker or stronger than van der Waals forces?
cards.definition: Stronger

cards.term: In which physical state is hydrogen bonding strongest?
cards.definition: Solid (weakest in gas)

cards.term: Give examples of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
cards.definition: HF, water, alcohols

cards.term: Give an example of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
cards.definition: o-Nitrophenol (H between two O atoms)
